population: Vietnamese general medicine students, Y4-Y6; equal year weighting until player population is known
construct: Condition recognition and basic understanding, independent of any puzzle clues or treatment details

curriculum: Repeated explicit core learning objectives across at least two undergraduate programmes
Explicit required disease topic or core problem in one undergraduate programme
Limited depth, optional coverage, or documented institutional variation
Predominantly advanced specialty teaching with positive supporting evidence
Documented postgraduate/subspecialty scope; no inference from search absence
exposure: Repeated encounters in several core placements
Usually encountered in a relevant core placement
Occasional encounter or substantial regional/seasonal variation
Unlikely firsthand encounter during ordinary placements
Exceptional encounter even at typical training hospitals
reinforcement: Repeated across core undergraduate resources and assessment blueprints
Dedicated undergraduate chapter/lecture or verified assessment objective
Mainly subspecialty literature; little generalist reinforcement
pattern: Most students know the canonical syndrome and basic mechanism
Standard presentation and basic mechanism usually familiar
Name recognized, but canonical syndrome or mechanism variably understood
Pattern generally requires additional specialty study
Recognition and basic understanding require niche knowledge
scope: Broad generalist recognition and initial assessment expected across core placements
Routine recognition/basic understanding within a core specialty
Generalist awareness expected, detailed understanding less consistent
Subspecialty-level entity or fine subtype distinction

warning: Weights, level boundaries and tiers are design hypotheses, not validated probabilities. Missing values are unknown, never proof of specialist scope.
